name: Gemcitabine plus CISplatin, Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma (Induction or Adjuvant)

source.nccn: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers (Nasopharynx)

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Gemcitabine plus cisplatin is the standard cytotoxic doublet for EBV-associated nasopharyngeal carcinoma, used as induction chemotherapy before chemoradiation for bulky stage III-IVA disease and as EBV-DNA-guided adjuvant chemotherapy. Not biomarker-selected beyond the nasopharyngeal indication; plasma EBV DNA guides adjuvant use.

premedications.name: CISplatin hydration and antiemetics
premedications.notes: IV hydration and high-emetic-risk antiemetic prophylaxis before cisplatin.

supportiveCare: Antiemetic prophylaxis: high emetic risk (cisplatin-containing); prophylaxis per emetogenicity tier.
Monitor for gemcitabine myelosuppression, particularly thrombocytopenia, before the day 8 dose.
G-CSF / febrile-neutropenia risk assessment per institutional practice.
monitoring: CBC before each dose (day 1 and day 8)
renal function (creatinine/GFR) before each cisplatin dose
audiometry / neuropathy assessment with cumulative cisplatin
plasma EBV DNA for response and adjuvant decision-making

doseModificationRules.condition: renal impairment or cytopenia on day 1
doseModificationRules.text: Review required. Protocol-specific delay/reduce criteria may apply; physician decides.
Hold or reduce the day 8 gemcitabine dose for significant cytopenia; physician decides.

drugs.name: Gemcitabine
drugs.notes: Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 IV on days 1 and 8, every 21 days. Standard gemcitabine dose in the nasopharyngeal gemcitabine-cisplatin doublet (general oncology reference). Check CBC before the day 8 dose.

provenance.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers (Nasopharynx)

drugs.name: CISplatin
drugs.notes: CISplatin 80 mg/m2 IV on day 1, every 21 days, with adequate hydration. ISMP tall-man applied. Standard platinum dose in the nasopharyngeal gemcitabine-cisplatin doublet (general oncology reference).

provenance.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers (Nasopharynx)
